text:
Artificial intelligence is influencing not only how students learn but also what educational institutions choose to teach. Traditional curricula are often reviewed periodically and may take years to change. In contrast, AI-related technologies are developing rapidly, creating pressure for schools and universities to update course content more frequently. Effective curriculum design must therefore balance new technical knowledge with enduring academic and human skills.

One significant change is the growing need for AI literacy. Students should understand how AI systems generate outputs, use data, and produce errors. They do not all need to become programmers, but they should be able to evaluate automated information, recognise possible bias, and use AI tools responsibly. These abilities are becoming relevant across subjects, including business, science, language, and the humanities.

AI can also assist educators in designing curricula. By analysing assessment results and learning patterns, AI systems may identify topics that students commonly misunderstand. Teachers can use this information to reorganise lessons, introduce additional practice, or provide alternative explanations. AI may also help generate examples and activities suited to different levels of ability.

However, curriculum decisions should not be driven entirely by technology. Schools may be tempted to prioritise immediately marketable AI skills while reducing attention to history, literature, ethics, and the arts. Such an approach would be narrow because students need cultural knowledge, moral reasoning, and communication skills to understand the broader effects of technology.

Curricula must also avoid becoming dependent on specific commercial tools. Platforms may change, disappear, or require expensive subscriptions. Educational programmes should therefore focus on transferable principles rather than temporary software features.

AI requires curricula to become more flexible and responsive. Nevertheless, education should not simply follow technological trends. A strong curriculum should combine AI literacy with critical thinking, ethical judgement, subject knowledge, and creativity. This balance will prepare students to use changing technologies without allowing those technologies to define the entire purpose of education.
